textbookText: Facts Some acidic oxides react with water to produce a mixture of two different acids. For example, 2NO2 + H2O → HNO2 +HNO3 P4O8 + 6H2O→ 2H3PO3 + 2H3PO4, etc.
Oxides which produce alkalies when dissolved in water are called basic oxides. Basic oxides when
treated with acid produce salt and water. Generally, these are the oxides of metals. For examples,
a) Oxides of group 1(alkali metals) and group 2 (alkaline earth metals except Be)
Li2O, Na2O, K2O, MgO, CaO, BaOetc are basic oxides. They are soluble in water.
b) Oxides of group d-block elements in the lower oxidation states like FeO, MnO, CuO, Ag2O, etc.
They are almost insoluble in water.
Reaction of oxides to prove the basic nature are given below:
BaO + H2O →Ba(OH)2(Barium hydroxide) FeO + H2O → Insoluble
(iii)Neutral Oxides Oxides which are neither acidic nor basic in nature are called neutral oxides. These oxides neither react with acid nor base. For example, N2O, H2O, NO, CO, etc.
(iv)Amphoteric Oxides Activity:11 Observe the reactions given below: ZnO + 2HCl →ZnCl2 + H2O ZnO + 2NaOH → Na2ZnO2 + H2O a. In which of the above reactions ZnO acts as acid?

Oxides which exhibit the properties of both acid and base are called amphoteric oxides. These oxides react with acid as well as base to produce salt and water. For example, ZnO, PbO, SnO, Al2O3, Ga2O3, Cr2O3, BeO, etc. Some reactions of oxides showing amphoteric nature: PbO + H2SO4 → PbSO4 + H2O

2. Classification of oxides on the basis of oxygen content (structural consideration)
On the basis of oxygen content oxides are of following types:

(i) Peroxide Activity:11 One of the commonly used chemicals for removing ear wax is given in the bottle. a. Write the molecular formula of this chemical. b. Why is this chemical called hydrogen peroxide?

Na2O2, BaO2, Li2O2, etc. are the examples of polyoxides commonly called peroxides. They contain peroxide unit (O22-). In these oxides the oxidation state of oxygen is -1. Peroxides when treated with dilute mineral acids produce hydrogen peroxide (H2O2). Na2O2 + H2SO4 →Na2SO4 + H2O2 Alkali metals and alkaline earth metals form peroxides of the type M2O2 and MO2, respectively where M is alkali and alkaline earth metal.

(ii) Mixed oxides Oxides which are the mixture of two or more oxides of same elements with different oxidation states are called mixed oxides or compound oxides. For example, Fe3O4, Mn3O4, Pb3O4, N2O4 etc. Fe3O4 is a mixture of FeO and Fe2O3 as it gives ferrous chloride and ferric chloride when treated with dilute hydrochloric acid.

Fe3O4 + 8HCl → FeCl2 + 2FeCl3 + 4H2O Similarly, Pb3O4 is a mixture of PbO and PbO2 as it gives lead nitrate and lead dioxide when treated with dilute nitric acid. Pb3O4 + 4HNO3 → 2Pb(NO3)2 + PbO2 + 2H2O Facts

a. Potassium superoxide (K2O) is used in space capsule, submarines and breathing masks. This is because K2O absorbs CO2 producing O2. 4K2O + 2CO2→2K2CO3 +O2 b. Pb3O4 is commonly known as red lead which is called 'Sindoor' in Nepali.
9.2.3: Hydrogen peroxide Activity:12 Observe the structure of molecule given and a. Write the molecular formula of compound? b. Name the structure of the molecule given.
Hydrogen peroxide is the most common peroxide of hydrogen having molecular formula H2O2. Pure hydrogen peroxide is a pale blue liquid slightly viscous than water.

Handling of hydrogen peroxide Hydrogen peroxide is a strong oxidizing and bleaching agent. Since, its high concentration is fatal therefore safety handling of H2O2 is required. Some of the safety measures required while using hydrogen peroxide are:

Hydrogen peroxide should be handled below its boiling point under reduced pressure. Hydrogen peroxide should be stored in an opaque bottle at low temperature and kept away from flammable substances. In laboratory hydrogen peroxide should be conducted in a properly functioning chemical fume hood whenever possible. Hydrogen peroxide is corrosive to skin and causes pulmonary irritations therefore its contact with the body should be avoided.
